title: Boolean encoding of a proposition
statement: For any type $\alpha$, proposition $p$ with a decision procedure, and function $f:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\to\alpha$, the value that is $f(\mathrm{true})$ when $p$ holds and $f(\mathrm{false})$ otherwise is $f(\mathrm{decide}(p))$, where $\mathrm{decide}(p)$ is true exactly when $p$ holds.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a proposition with a decision procedure
$f$ maps Boolean values to elements of $\alpha$
